FIS trails in Galtür

The FIS trails in Galtür offer challenging courses on homologated tracks within a stunning high-alpine setting. The trails are arranged in two loops from the western end of Galtür: one heads towards Wirl, while the other extends to the southern end of Galtür and the Jambach. The high alpine surroundings and the views of surrounding peaks, make these trails unique. The L.6 serves as the main trail, while L.6.1, L.6.2 and L.6.3 are variations with different lengths and levels of difficulty. Note: Trails may be temporarily closed for training or competitions.

L L1
Samnaun – Dorf – Ravaisch

This 1.6-kilometre trail runs from Samnaun Dorf over the meadows of Motnaida to Clis da Ravaisch and back. It offers gentle climbs in scenic surroundings.

Difference in altitude
51 hm
Length
1.6 km
Difficulty
Easy
Status
Closed

The Samnaun – Dorf – Ravaisch trail starts and ends in Samnaun Dorf near Votlas. This 1.6-kilometre track for classic and skating styles gently descends over the meadows of Motnaida towards Clis da Ravaisch and loops back. With a total ascent of 51 metres, this varied route is perfect for beginners and offers a tranquil winter experience in scenic surroundings.

L L2
Samnaun-Plan – Samnaun-Laret

The 2-kilometre trail runs parallel to the Schergenbach from Samnaun-Laret to Samnaun-Plan and back. With just 23 metres of elevation gain, it’s perfect for short, relaxed outings.

Difference in altitude
23 hm
Length
2 km
Difficulty
Easy
Status
Closed

The Samnaun-Plan – Samnaun-Laret trail begins at the valley road bridge in Samnaun-Laret and runs parallel to the Schergenbach stream. Spanning 2 kilometres, this track for classic and skating styles leads to the small hamlet of Samnaun-Plan before looping back. With just 23 metres of elevation gain, this trail is perfect for a short and leisurely outing in a picturesque winter setting.

M L
Opening Trail

Thanks to snow farming, two specially prepared opening trails at Sedlsee with a total length of 3,2 kilometres, offer ideal conditions for an early start to winter. Situated at an altitude of around 1,700 to 1,800 metres, the trails are suitable for both classic and skating techniques. Whether you're an ambitious athlete, part of a training group or a recreational cross-country skier, the stunning Silvretta mountain scenery provides the perfect backdrop for the start of the season.

  • Opening hours: Daily from 08:00 to 17:00
  • Training slots: 08:00 - 10:30, 10:30 - 13:00 and 14:00 - 16:30
Note:

The trail entrance is at the parking lot at Galtür toll station
